title: Workmanship Warranties Field Inspection Standard: Determining Coverage
content:
**Standard.** Where a Workmanship Warranties plan requires an inspection, a network inspection decides coverage before any remedy, offered within the plan's inspection scheduling business days of the report, with the plan's inspection photo count and, where the plan includes a structural measurement at inspection, a structural measurement. A concern is covered only when all of these hold:

1. its kind is one the plan covers: workmanship defects where the plan covers workmanship; paint defects where the plan covers paint defects; fading where the plan covers paint fade; leaks and wind noise where the plan covers water leaks and wind noise; panel gaps where the plan covers panel fit; edge stress cracks where the plan covers stress cracks; a spreading repaired chip where the plan covers chip spread; a calibration fault where the plan covers calibration faults and the odometer is within the plan's calibration mileage limit of the odometer at issue; an installed mechanical part within the plan's mechanical parts months and mechanical parts miles; an installed electrical part within the plan's electrical parts months; structural failure where the plan covers structural integrity; corrosion where the plan covers corrosion;
2. it lies in the area of the source work;
3. its cause is not one of the plan's excluded causes; and
4. it does not concern an excluded customer-supplied part or declined calibration.

The first exclusion that applies is recorded as the exclusion code. A concern was reported on the coverage before it is inspected.

## Condition before an inspection is recorded

A concern was reported on the coverage before it is inspected. The evidence is the company's record of that concern's report on the same coverage, identified by the coverage and the concern number; each inspection is of one reported concern.

## What an inspection records

| Item | Content |
|---|---|
| Inspection date | The date of the inspection |
| Concern | The concern number inspected |
| Determination | covered or not covered |
| Exclusion | The first exclusion that applies; none when covered |
| Center | The network center that inspected |

## The four tests as a table

| Kind covered by the plan (with its limit) | In the area of the source work | Cause not excluded | Not an excluded customer-supplied part or declined calibration | Determination |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| yes | yes | yes | yes | covered |
| no | any | any | any | not covered |
| any | no | any | any | not covered |
| any | any | no | any | not covered |
| any | any | any | no | not covered |

Because a concern is covered only when all four hold, failing any one of them makes it not covered.

## Hypothetical example

Under a Collision Lifetime Workmanship Warranty whose plan covers installed mechanical parts for 12 months and 12000 miles, a mechanical part concern is inspected 14 months after the issued date. The part is outside the plan's mechanical parts months, so the first test fails and the concern is not covered; the first exclusion that applies is recorded as the exclusion code.
